Hand in the four deliverables independently in 90 minutes, including the reference and three counterexamples; there is no real venue, customer, funds, account, or equipment.

Fit signals｜O*NET focus points: continuous contact with others (87% continuous contact), daily face-to-face discussions (85% every day), daily decisions affecting others and organizational resources (64% every day), must be very precise or highly accurate “extremely important” (84%) and “very important” (16%), continuous or almost continuous standing (75%), continuous or almost continuous repetitive motions (77%), need to deal with unpleasant or angry or impolite people every day (67%), daily time pressure from strict deadlines (56%), working with a work group or team extremely important (41%), respondents choosing a regular schedule (89%). If you can stay transaction-accurate and patient with customers throughout high-frequency change-making at peak times and in the slot machine area, this occupation's daily demands are closer to your working style.

Caution signals｜O*NET also shows: consequences of error “extremely serious” (14%) and “very serious” (13%) and “serious” (24%) and “fairly serious” (14%), but a considerable share consider it “not at all serious” (35%); decision freedom “some” (34%) and “limited” (30%) and “very little” (17%); competition level “extremely competitive” (16%) and “highly competitive” (16%) and “moderately competitive” (34%); physical proximity “very close” (22%) and “moderately close (within arm's reach)” (56%); email never 67%, at least weekly but not daily 16%; sitting never 50%, less than half 25%, about half 16%. This occupation centers on cash and chips and tickets and exchange and reconciliation and customer service: one missing identity or age verification, one large or unusual transaction not identified and reported, one amount or change or payout error, one case of drawer accounts not matching actuals or differences privately balanced, or one missing authorization form or signature or transaction record can cause financial loss and compliance penalties and license risk; moreover, gambling is strictly restricted by law in mainland China, and before getting involved the law and authorization of the location must be verified. If you find it hard to stay transaction-accurate and to keep reporting over the long term in a highly regulated and highly repetitive cash environment, these should be treated as real costs requiring careful weighing.

Direct answer｜The work of gambling change persons and booth cashiers can be broadly divided into three categories. First, currency and chip and ticket exchange and payout: exchange currency and credit cards and tickets and chips and tokens with each other for patrons and make change, sell chips and tokens and tickets to patrons or to other workers, listen for jackpot bells and pay out to winners, obtain the customer's signature on the receipt when the prize exceeds the amount held in the slot machine, and calculate the value for players based on chip wins and losses. Second, counting and reconciliation and bookkeeping: count cash and audit cash drawers, verify records of currency exchange and authorization forms and transaction reconciliation, reconcile the daily transaction summary to balance the books, and issue the reserve to change persons at the start of the shift according to procedures. Third, booth and slot machine area service and compliance records: operate a booth in the slot machine area and provide service to patrons, check identification to verify player age, maintain booth security according to the rules, accept credit applications and verify credit references to provide check-cashing authorization or establish house credit accounts, maintain accurate records and clean the casino area, and identify and report anomalies according to jurisdictional and employer procedures. The three categories of work link in cycles: verify customer identity and age — handle exchange and change and payout — issue and recall the reserve — count drawers and reconcile the summary — record and report anomalies.

O*NET occupational profile highlights｜The official scope of O*NET-SOC 41-2012.00 “Gambling Change Persons and Booth Cashiers” is: Exchange coins, tokens, and chips for patrons' money. May issue payoffs and obtain customer's signature on receipt. May operate a booth in the slot machine area and furnish change persons with money bank at the start of the shift, or count and audit money in drawers. Of the 13 tasks given in the occupational profile, 6 are core tasks: keep accurate records of currency exchange and authorization forms and transaction reconciliation; exchange currency and credit and tickets or casino chips for patrons and make change; count cash and audit cash drawers; check identification to verify player age; maintain booth security according to the rules; reconcile the daily transaction summary to balance the books. There are another 7 supplemental tasks: obtain the customer's signature on the receipt when the prize exceeds the amount held in the slot machine; calculate the chip value of player wins or losses; accept credit applications and verify credit references to provide check-cashing authorization or establish house credit accounts; furnish change persons with a reserve at the start of each shift; listen for jackpot bells and issue payouts to winners; sell casino chips and tokens or tickets to patrons or to other workers for resale to patrons; clean the casino area.

entries.answer: According to O*NET-SOC 41-2012.00, this occupation exchanges coins and tokens and chips for patrons' money; may issue payoffs and obtain the customer's signature on the receipt; may operate a booth in the slot machine area and furnish change persons with a reserve at the start of the shift, or count and audit cash drawers. The work includes exchanging currency and credit and tickets or casino chips for patrons and making change, counting cash and auditing cash drawers, checking identification to verify player age, maintaining booth security according to the rules, reconciling the daily transaction summary to balance the books, obtaining receipt signatures when the prize exceeds the amount held in the machine, calculating the chip value of player wins and losses, accepting credit applications and verifying credit references, issuing the reserve at shift start, listening for jackpot bells and paying out, selling chips and tokens and tickets, and maintaining accurate records and cleaning the casino area. What this page describes is a legal position in jurisdictions such as the United States that allow licensed gambling; in mainland China, apart from the state-approved lotteries issued in accordance with the law, gambling and operating casinos are strictly prohibited by the Criminal Law and other laws.

entries.answer: The core difference lies in object and output: this occupation takes the currency and chips and tickets and payout and cash drawer at the change booth and slot machine area as its object and completes exchange and change and payout and counting and auditing, with the output being verified and recorded exchange and payout and bookkeeping records; gambling cage workers produce the cage general ledger and credit and check cashing and bookkeeping; gambling dealers produce table game operation and chip receipt and payment; gambling and sports book writers and runners produce wager acceptance and odds verification and payout records; first-line supervisors of gambling services workers produce shifts and on-site supervision and performance and compliance enforcement; gambling managers produce venue operations and licensing and compliance management; gambling surveillance officers and gambling investigators produce surveillance and investigation and evidence. The focus of objects and outputs differs and duties may cross over, and the authority for release and credit and fund handling cannot be carried over across positions. This occupation includes credit checking as a supplemental task, which does not exclude real authorization judgment within the definition.

subject.name: Gambling Change Persons and Booth Cashiers
subject.summary: Gambling Change Persons and Booth Cashiers (O*NET-SOC 41-2012.00, Gambling Change Persons and Booth Cashiers) exchange money and chips for patrons at the change booth and in the slot machine area of a licensed gambling establishment: exchange coins and tokens and chips for patrons' money, exchange money and credit and tickets or casino chips for patrons and make change, and may issue payoffs and obtain the customer's signature on the receipt; may operate a booth in the slot machine area and furnish change persons with a money bank at the start of the shift, or count and audit money in drawers. The work includes counting cash and auditing cash drawers, checking identification to verify player age, maintaining booth security according to the rules, reconciling daily transaction summaries to balance the books, obtaining customer signatures when over the limit, calculating the chip value of player wins and losses, accepting credit applications and verifying credit references, listening for jackpot bells and paying out, selling chips and tokens and tickets, and maintaining accurate records and cleaning the casino area. Official definition text: Exchange coins, tokens, and chips for patrons' money. May issue payoffs and obtain customer's signature on receipt. May operate a booth in the slot machine area and furnish change persons with money bank at the start of the shift, or count and audit money in drawers.
